entities.summary:
The Battle of Blue Waters was a pivotal medieval conflict that took place in 1362-1363 between the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and the Golden Horde, a kipchak khanate. This battle marked a significant turning point in the history of Eastern Europe, as it halted the Mongol expansion into the region and allowed the Lithuanians to secure their borders. The battle's outcome had far-reaching consequences, as it paved the way for the rise of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania as a major power in the region.

The battle itself was a clash of two mighty forces, with the Lithuanians employing their traditional tactics of feigned retreats and ambushes to great effect. The Golden Horde, meanwhile, was led by the ambitious khan Tokhtamysh, who sought to expand his empire's reach into Eastern Europe. Despite being outnumbered, the Lithuanians were able to hold off the Golden Horde's initial attacks, before launching a decisive counterattack that sent the Mongols reeling.

The battle's legacy can be seen in the subsequent rise of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania as a major power in the region. Under the leadership of Grand Duke Algirdas, the Lithuanians went on to expand their territories, incorporating the lands of modern-day Belarus, Ukraine, and parts of Poland. This expansion had a lasting impact on the region, shaping the course of Eastern European history for centuries to come.

As the Polish historian, Józef Szujski, noted, 'The Battle of Blue Waters was a turning point in the history of Lithuania, marking the beginning of a new era of expansion and growth for the Grand Duchy.'
